newsitem.title: USA: Convicted murdered scheduled to die in Arizona.
newsitem.headline: Convicted murdered scheduled to die in Arizona.

text.p: William Lyle Woratzeck, who murdered a mentally-impaired woman in 1980, is scheduled to be put to death by lethal injection early Wednesday.

Barring any last-minute stays, prison officials said Woratzeck will receive the fatal dose shortly after midnight Tuesday while strapped to a table in the state prison complex in Florence, Ariz., about 60 miles southeast of Phoenix.
Woratzeck, 51, would be the eighth person executed in Arizona since the state resumed capital punishment in 1992. The last execution was in January.
He has been facing the death penalty for more than 16 years for killing Linda Louise Leslie, a 36-year-old who had rented an apartment from him in Casa Grande, Ariz.
Authorities said Woratzeck broke into Leslie's room in the small southern Arizona community in the early hours of March 6, 1980.
Prosecutors said he beat her with a hammer, stabbed her three times and strangled her. He set the residence on fire, but not before robbing Leslie of $107, they said.
Woratzeck was arrested one week later for breaking into a nursery the same night. While in jail, he was charged with the murder and several other offences.
He was sentenced to death in October 1980 for the killing after a five-day jury trial.
An appeal to the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals was denied last September and the U.S. Supreme Court in April also refused to grant him reconsideration.

His attorneys have maintained that Woratzeck is innocent and that he did not receive adequate legal representation. They add that even if he did kill Leslie, the case does not warrant the death penalty.
To the end, his relatives also have said Woratzeck did not commit the murder.
